Could the requesting teacher, the instructional technology specialist, and the business-office manager please share any relevant findings?

transcript.text: Dr. Monroe, I should share an important finding from a classroom trial I conducted this week. I tested the setup with the enrolled section, and the results showed that all 12 students need simultaneous stations — each student requires one laptop and one USB microphone. That means the current proposal for 10 laptops would not be sufficient for the class size, and USB microphones are not included in the request. I recorded these results in my classroom planning log, but I realize now that the log was not attached to the capital request.

transcript.text: Dr. Monroe, I need to share the findings from my network and privacy review. I completed the review this week, and the commercial cloud music platform requested in the proposal cannot be used with student accounts. Instead, the district-managed SoundLab EDU platform is approved for use, but it requires managed student accounts plus a security configuration record. I closed the technology review ticket this week, but it has not yet been linked to the purchasing request, so this information may not have been visible in the proposal materials.

The grant will fund this project, but only up to exactly $6,800, and only if the purchase order is issued by August 20, 2026. This funding note has not yet been added to the proposal, so it would not have been visible in the proposal materials. Additionally, the grant's August 20, 2026 purchase order deadline is earlier than the proposed September 1, 2026 installation date, so the timeline would need to be adjusted.
